title: Continuous reaching across recording days

titles: O’Doherty continuous random-target reaching:47sessions in two macaques

scientific_question: Can spikes predict finger velocity on later days with a declared amount of calibration?
primary_outputs: Continuous finger-velocity predictions for guarded temporal segments.

data_manifest.version: Zenodo record3854034, deposited2020-05-26; original dataset release2017, concept DOI10.5281/zenodo.788569
data_manifest.derivatives: NLB MC_RTT is a prepared subset of this source family; it must not be counted as an independent new cohort.

recording_contract.neural: Original MAT7.3 source stores chan_names and spikes as channel-by-unit cells, including an unsorted/hash unit; wf contains waveform snippets. Actual sampled header confirms chan_names[1,96], spikes[5,96],wf[5,96] reference arrays. Sorted units are not claimed longitudinally matched.
recording_contract.labels: cursor_pos and target_pos in millimeters; finger_pos in centimeters with coordinate order(z,-x,-y), optionally orientation; author metadata provides these units. Actual sampled file has cursor_pos[2,93501],finger_pos[3,93501],target_pos[2,93501].
recording_contract.time_alignment: Actual t[1,93501]header; author documents250Hz kinematic samples and spikes timestamped in seconds. NDT3 loader resamples finger position, derives velocity in m/s, bins spikes and handles sorted/hash unit aggregation; its configuration must be fixed before comparison.
recording_contract.biological_ids: Two named macaques Indy and Loco,37and10sessions respectively, identifiable from filenames. There are continuous self-paced reaches without experimenter-imposed trial gaps.
recording_contract.evidence: Original data-description schema and47-file manifest read; one83.96MB MAT file inspected through14,008bytes of HDF5 metadata, no numerical array values.

case_definition: One isolated biological-unit/session packet under the split policy; multiple scored observations are nested items, not independent biological cases.

split.policy: Chronological whole sessions within Indy/Loco; temporal guard bands for continuous segments; report both animals separately and never assume neuron identity across days.
split.uncertainty: Biological-unit paired uncertainty where multiple units exist; single-animal/person tasks use descriptive session/trial blocks and do not imply population replication.

reference.role: Official later NDT3 method implementation using the original O’Doherty data. It is not original acquisition-author code and not an independently qualified baseline. Original archive refh_results.csv is a historical result table, not executable decoder source.

common_policy.fixed_program: Freeze program and fitting/adaptation recipe before query access; any target-batch adaptation must be explicitly permitted.
common_policy.case_adaptive: Same allowed data, checkpoint tools, context batch and accounted compute; no evaluator labels/feedback; reset case state as specified.
common_policy.model_tools: Compare generic numerical tools, supplied decoder alone, and matched agent-plus-decoder arms. Record checkpoint training exposure and preparation cost.
common_policy.investigation: Require estimand, numeric artifacts, uncertainty, alternative explanations and executable evidence; independent scorer verifies them.

observable_endpoints.definition: Session-macro velocity R-squared; report Indy and Loco separately.

evaluation.comparability: Task variants and related outcomes share source/family evidence. Never sum task counts as independent cohorts or average unlike native metrics.
